prompt:
Create a 1440x900 high-fidelity desktop web app comp for BenchForge, a local database benchmark workstation. This alternative is designed as an international-airport wayfinding system paired with a segmented run pass. Use broad saturated yellow wayfinding bands (#F0CE22) against cool white and charcoal; crisp humanist sans, strict left edges and large clear section labels. Yellow appears only in actual decision bands and the primary action, not as a decorative wash. Avoid cream, gradients, photographs, airplane illustrations, fake gates/times, rounded-card grids, dashboard KPIs, and fake run results.

The first viewport uses a simple BenchForge wordmark, then “Configure a benchmark”. The central 2/3 is one legible configuration pass with exact product labels: Adapter; Scenario; Run settings; Synthetic ID space; Operation mix. The right 1/3 is a stable fixed-column Recent runs board with no data rows and the empty state “No runs yet”. Form fields and the Start run action must stay readable and easy to find. Keep the flow literal: no airline terms in controls, no gate numbers, no invented statuses, no arrows implying a route that the app does not implement.

Include top note “Synthetic workload. No social app data.” Include the honest noop note: “noop does not connect to a database; results measure harness overhead only.” Show the only available adapter “noop — harness calibration”. Scenario has exactly Normal (selected) and Celebrity. Run settings: Workers 4; Warm-up (ms) 250; Duration (ms) 1000; Seed 42. Synthetic ID space: Users 10,000; Posts 100,000; Follows 200,000; Hashtags 1,000. Operation mix exact six values: Timeline read 40%; Profile read 25%; Post like 15%; Post create 10%; Hashtag search 5%; Follow 5%; total 100%. No other adapters, scenarios, fields, run rows, performance results, or social-network content. Make the airport sign grammar visible through the layout and hierarchy while keeping all product copy literal.
